Hi Will — thanks for the sample and the clear signal on burst shape. Looping in Karthik, Monica, and Dylan from SE/CS/Runtime to map out a concrete list. High-level suggestions up front so the sync can be tactical:

1) Batching: target dynamic batching with a soft cap of 32 tokens-per-batch and an aggressive time-window of 6 ms for latency-sensitive endpoints; for cheaper conversational backfills, allow batch sizes up to 128 where tail latency is acceptable.

2) KV/prefix caching: since you have a frequently reused prefix, enable per-customer KV caching with conservative TTLs to start (30s) and evaluate hit-rate after a 48-hour profiling window; if hit-rate > 35% we can extend to 2–5m.

3) Quantization profiles: recommend two parallel variants for initial tuning — q4f (faster, slight quality drop) and int8-approx (higher compress, good for throughput). We'll A/B them on a small sample set.

4) Routing/canary policy: start 100% hosted -> 5% dedicated for canary (traffic-split by session-id hashing), hold for 24 hours then 20% if metrics look good. Automatic rollback on >5% error/quality regression.

I'll draft a one-page warmup checklist and bring the tuning-playbook to the call. Are you available 11:00–11:45am PT tomorrow?

—Hannah

Hi all — quick technical notes to bring into the call; I'll share a short tuning-playbook.pdf during the meeting. TL;DR: predictable knobs we control and how they map to cost/latency/quality.

- Batching: for your prompt length distribution, set dynamic batcher target sizes at 16 (low-latency) and 96 (throughput path). Use sequence-length bucketing to avoid wasted compute. Expect median latency improvement of ~18–25% at the 96 path, but 95th pct will increase.

- KV prefetch: prefetch the first 2 KV entries for any session with repeated prefix; track miss rate metric 'kv.hit_rate' and evaluate after 24–48 hours. Conservative TTL 30s minimizes staleness; increasing to 2–5m yields diminishing returns unless hit_rate > 40%.

- Quantization: start with q4f on a shadow variant for 10% of traffic; run our automated evals on your prompt set (we'll run A/B on Rouge/EM-like metrics you provide). int8-approx saves ~1.6–1.9x cost but watch for hallucination delta on long prompt contexts.

- Routing & canary: recommend hashing on account_id for sticky routing. Canary plan: 95% hosted / 5% dedicated for 24h, then 80/20 after manual review. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, token-cost per request, and "generation_quality.delta" (we'll provide a simple rubric).

Attachments I will bring: tuning-playbook.pdf, canary-mop-up.docx (rollback steps and escalation contacts).

Happy to discuss in 11:00 PT slot.
